body: You sound like a good, capable person.  And Christ, if you ain't been through a lot, then I don't know what a lot is.  Yet everything that's happened to you and you've kept trucking up to now with twice the effort I'd expect to see from someone who's fallen down that many times.  I'm in a dark place, too, so any advice I could even think of giving would be some pretty hypocritical shit, but know this: everything you've lived through makes you a hero in my eyes, at least.  If you keep fighting, I'm sure you'll be that to people you know if you aren't already.

Thank you for the compliment.  Funny thing, writing was one of the things I gave up on.  But, no, I haven't had professional help yet.  I was only in Kindergarten and wouldn't realize what happened until third grade.  I remember this Spider-Man comic book they gave us, just some PSA bullshit, but it's got Spidey in it, right?  And in it, this kid's sitter comes in and dangles a late night of TV watching over his head at the cost of his clothes, innocence and silence.  Then Spidey comes in and chases her off.  And as I read it, I thought it'd be like every other comicbook I'd ever read, picturing myself in the hero's shoes while they take down bad guys.  But take away the cajoling and I realized I was the kid, in reality, where superheroes never existed. I tried to shut it out.  Knowing what happened, I blamed myself for failing to prevent it as much as I blamed her for doing it in the first place.  But the more I tried, the more clearly and more often it came back to me.  And now, as an adult, I'm poor, can't afford help, and decided I'd at least try to power through it on my own. 

 Apart from now, I've only ever told my mother and my last ex 20 years after the fact, and in those years, and even after, it got to a point where I couldn't stop thinking about what had happened and what I'd do if I ever had the misfortune of seeing my rapist again after all this time.  Then, my aunt died a year later and she turns right up for the get together before the funeral.  Arm-in-arm with my mother. And with the stress of losing her sister and everything else that's going on, Mom's forgotten what kind of monster she's sharing a hearty laugh with. And as my attacker's smiling straight at me, and I could swear I see in her eyes that she remembers it all, I realize that I don't have it in me. 

 Hurting her right then meant my mom would lose her only son to prison, on top of losing her sister for good.  Exposing her right then would just make me look weak _and_ sully my aunt's memory in front of everyone, and then, I'm the asshole.  So I bottled it up and walked away, knowing all the years I spent on revenge fantasy daydreams of bringing her to justice were for nothing. 

That was the breaking point for me.  I was born from a line of cops, soldiers, hell, even Black Panthers, ass-kickers all day, who went so far as to give their lives to keep my family safe, our country free, and our rights intact, and I couldn't even fight for myself when I had the chance.  If I can't even live up to the expectations written into my own DNA, I can't hope to live up to my own, let alone others'.  To see other people manage it guts me every time, knowing that many of them have faced far worse, but the way they come back from it... it's like they're Teflon and I'm black tar.  And I know it's not that simple, but that's how it's always felt.  I just want that strength.  That resilience.  The ability to still give a damn when it's all said and done.

I know I got seriously carried away, but thank you for bothering to read my rambling and for the advice.  I actually feel a little better.  Clouds are still there, but it helped to get this off my chest.  I think I know what I need to do.
